candidates.computation_change_reason: MAHL is expressly conditional ('if applicable'); whether MAHL applies changes which numeric limit basis governs (A) and whether headworks/influent loading monitoring is required versus report-only (B).

Identifies daily-average effluent numeric limits in µg/L with a footnote reference; interpretation of the limit values, units, averaging basis, or footnote \3 changes which enforceable limit is compared to reported measurements.

Requires influent concentration reporting in the table; whether influent monitoring is an enforceable obligation versus informational reporting changes monitoring applicability (B) and what constitutes adequate evidence when influent results are absent (C).

Specifies effluent concentration reporting in µg/L for comparison against effluent limits; interpretation affects which measurements are subject to limit comparison (A) and which effluent monitoring events are required (B).

Conditions both influent and effluent reporting to dates actually sampled rather than fixed calendar periods; different readings change when monitoring is required (B) and whether missing data reflects non-required periods versus inadequate evidence (C).

The *T annotation on listed metals may denote a toxics or special-status category; its meaning affects whether numeric limits apply, which monitoring rules govern these parameters, and how no-result or conditional cases are classified.

Unlike other pollutants where *T appears on the same line, Molybdenum places *T on a separate line; ambiguity in how *T attaches to this parameter could change limit applicability, monitoring obligations, and missing-evidence handling for Molybdenum.

Footnote marker \4 appears in the segment without its defining text; its operative meaning (e.g., no-data codes, exclusions, or conditional non-requirements) would change how periods without ordinary numeric results are classified.
